newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STABILITY SEEN IN T-BILL MARKET.
newsitem.headline: STABILITY SEEN IN T-BILL MARKET.

text.p: Falling yields on Lithuanian government Treasury bills indicate stability on the market and confidence in Lithuania's approach to monetary policy, officials and analysts said on Monday.

Yields have been falling in recent weeks as foreign investors have returned to the market after their nerves were rattled in the wake of last October's parliamentary elections, when the new government said it would scrap the currency board.
The government has long since backed away from its hardline stance on the currency board, which pegs the litas to the dollar at a rate of four to one.
The central bank has developed a plan which calls for the board's replacement over the next two to three years.
"This (falling yields) indicates that there is macroeconomic stability on the market," said Margarita Starkeviciute, head of research at the Central Depository.
"Investors do not expect any changes in monetary policy this year," she said.
"Without confidence, the yields won't fall," said Ramunas Lygis, head of the Finance Ministry's market operations division.
"Foreigners have come back to the market," Lygis said, adding that a slump in the equities market has also contributed to growing demand for government debt.
Lithuania's bourse has been in a slump since the steam was let out of a bull market earlier in the year.
The average yield at Monday's auction for 91-day paper rose a wisp to 9.19 percent from 9.18 percent but the spread between high and low yields narrowed, indicating stabilisation.
